newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end off as market searches for trend.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end off as market searches for trend.

text.p: Dutch shares started the week with a loss, as nerves over the market's direction and a weak start of trade on Wall Street took their toll.
The main share index, the AEX, closed off 1.39 points at 979.35, slipping in the afternoon after touching a high of 988.77 earlier during the session.
Dealers said some market players had got wary of the underlying market direction.
"There's some fear in the market, people are no longer that convinced, they're looking for a direction," one dealer said.
"But there's still a majority of bulls," another said.
Technical analysts said the AEX index still had upside potential, but noted a slowdown in momentum recently.
Music and entertainment group PolyGram closed up six guilders at 118.00.
"Apparently, Mr. Bean is doing very well, and the stock was also upgraded by a broker on Friday last week," one dealer said.
KLM added 3.40 guilders to 76.40 in brisk trade.
"It's speculation over the figure, but also hopes for some interesting announcements of the new chairman," one dealer said.
"There's some massive gambling going on in that stock, just like in Wolters Kluwer," another said.
Both companies are due to report on Tuesday.
Analysts forecast a Q1 net profit from ordinary operations of 115 million guilders for KLM, down from 271 last year.
Wolters Kluwer H1 net from ordinary ops is seen up 19 percent to 245 million guilders, boosted by the higher dollar.
The share closed 10.10 higher at 283.00 guilders after peaking at 297.70 guilders, with options also being very active.
Hoogovens, reporting first half earnings on Wednesday, climbed 3.70 to 138.50 guilders in brisk volume.
"The market is clearly very positive on those results," one dealer said.
Financial stocks showed a meagre performance with Aegon losing 3.30 to 153.20 guilders and Amev off 1.50 to 91.20 guilders.
ING shed 1.20 to 98.70, while ABN AMRO closed down 80 cents at 47.50 guilders.
"We have bonds doing not so good, that trickles onto financial stocks," one dealer said.
Dealers were unable to explain the six percent rise of builder Heidemij to 21.50 guilders.
"With the entire market booming, that stock had become a laggard," one said.
